key_insight: A morphology-aware deep learning model can use tissue structure on whole-slide images to predict 5-year colorectal cancer survival, with strongest signals emerging from adipose and stroma as well as tumor regions.
clinical_relevance: If validated further, this approach could help stratify colorectal cancer patients by recurrence/mortality risk using routinely collected pathology slides.
method: Weakly supervised multiple-instance learning on H&E whole-slide images
Uses tissue morphology labels as structural supervision plus contrastive learning
Adds diversity regularization and gated-attention pooling to improve prognostic representation
evidence_signal: The model was developed on Alliance/CALGB 89803 (n=424), analyzed with TCGA-COAD/READ (n=562), and externally evaluated on SurGen (n=218), reaching AUCs up to 0.678 externally and 0.70 in pooled out-of-fold ensemble testing.
watch_item: Performance is promising but still modest and should be treated cautiously until prospectively validated across broader institutions, scanners, and pathology workflows.
paper_title: Morphology-aware deep learning predicts colorectal cancer survival from whole-slide images
